name: Monocle
tagline: Dim everything around your active window so you can focus without closing other apps.
description:
Monocle is a focus utility for macOS that dims everything except the window currently in use. It keeps apps and windows open, but lowers their visual presence so a crowded desktop becomes easier to work in without manually hiding or rearranging it.

Activate the effect with its gesture, work in the active window, and move the cursor when you need to reveal the rest of the screen. This is useful for writing, browsing, reading, and any task where peripheral windows create visual distraction even when they are not actively demanding attention.

## Features

- Dim inactive windows while keeping them open and unchanged.
- Use a mouse-shake activation gesture and cursor reveal effect to switch attention quickly.
- Work with Stage Manager and app groups according to the current release.
- Keep a lightweight focus overlay instead of closing windows or changing a workspace layout.

## Where it fits

Monocle fits people whose desktop becomes visually noisy while they still need several apps open. It is an especially good companion for writing, research, and focused browsing.

It will not prevent a distracting site or app from being opened. Use a true blocker for access restrictions, and consider reduced-motion or accessibility preferences before relying on cursor-triggered effects.

## Privacy and requirements

Monocle needs Accessibility access to identify and respond to the active window, and visual effects may require additional display-related permission on current macOS releases. Its privacy documentation is less prominent than its product information, so avoid assuming that every diagnostic or update request is local. Test exclusions for calls, presentations, and full-screen work before leaving it active.

## Pricing

Monocle costs $9 for a one-time license.
